kinds.fence: ```lang file=path lines=10-24 [scroll], or several ```lang step blocks
kinds.use: specific code, read from the project
kinds.point: #L12, #L12-18, [label](#L12 "exact text"); with steps, #step-2 moves to that version and later line cues count in it
kinds.reveal: lines up to the last range pointed at
kinds.format: `scroll` keeps long code (up to 400 lines) at reading size and scrolls to each cued range, dimming the rest. Consecutive blocks marked `step` are versions of one piece of code on one slide; `#step-N` morphs to version N. Code keeps its reading size: lines too long for it wrap, continuing under their own indent, so only too many lines make code small (text_too_small). Wrapped lines still read worse than an excerpt that fits (code_too_wide).

kinds.fence: ```lang old / ```lang new, ```diff, or ```diff file=path rev=A (or A..B, or A...B: B against where it branched off A)
kinds.format: The two sides show next to each other, stacked in portrait. A diff too wide to show side by side at reading size stacks, before above after, and lines still too long wrap under their own indent; both read worse than a hunk that fits (diff_too_wide).

kinds.point: #node-id (a flowchart node, sequence participant or state), [label](# "node label"), #a->b->c to send a dot along those edges (flowcharts), or #Sender->>Receiver for a message in a sequence diagram (the first between them; add quoted text to pick another)
kinds.reveal: flowchart nodes in source order, edges once both ends show
kinds.example:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  req[Request] --> cache{Cached?}
  cache -->|no| db[Database]
```

kinds.point: #row-2, or {#id} at the end of a row's last cell
kinds.reveal: rows up to the last one pointed at
kinds.example:
| Store | Speed |
|---|---|
| Memory | fast {#mem} |
| Disk | slow {#disk} |

kinds.fence: - items, 1. items, - [x] / - [ ] checklist items; .cards, .steps, .stack, .timeline (dates as bold titles) on the heading, or .quiz there to ask the viewer to pick one answer; `- :icon: **Title**: text` leads an item with an icon
kinds.use: parallel parts, options, a procedure, layers of a stack, a checklist, dated events, a question that checks the viewer understood
kinds.point: #id from {#id}, or the bold title lowercased with hyphens; quiz choices #a, #b, #c, #d unless an item has its own {#id}
kinds.reveal: items up to the last one pointed at; checklist ticks draw as their item is pointed at; a quiz shows its answer when a written cue points at the right choice
kinds.format: Quiz: `.quiz` on the heading and two to four `- [ ]` choices with exactly one `- [x]` (quiz_shape), shown lettered A to D; the viewer can click one. Only a written cue at the right choice, such as [B](#b), shows the answer (the right choice turns green, the others dim, a wrong pick is marked); cues inferred from saying the choices aloud do not, and with no cue it shows as the narration ends. Ask in the first paragraph, then a {pause=3} paragraph, during which a bar runs down, then point at the answer and say why the tempting wrong choice is wrong (quiz_reveal). Example: `## Which call retries? {.quiz}`, then `- [ ] fetch`, `- [x] send`, `- [ ] close`.
kinds.example:
- :zap: **Memory**: fast, gone on restart {#memory}
- :hard-drive: **Disk**: survives restarts {#disk}

kinds.use: a screenshot or plot from the project
kinds.point: #, or #@left,top,width,height in percent of the picture; add {.zoom} after the link to zoom onto it

kinds.use: numbers: before and after, shares, a trend
kinds.point: bar and hbar: #label (the bar's label, lowercased with hyphens); line: #series
kinds.reveal: bars or series in source order
kinds.format: bar: one `label: value` line per bar; for grouped bars, a `series: a, b` line first, then `label: 1, 2`. hbar: like bar, one series, for long labels. line: an `x: …` line first, then one `series: v1, v2, …` line per series, with as many values as x values. At most 12 bars or series. A `note x: text` line (or `note series/x: text` for one series of a line chart, `note label: text` for a bar) adds a callout; cue it as #note-1, #note-2 in order.
kinds.example:
```chart bar title="p95 latency" unit="ms"
series: before, after
read: 420, 180
write: 610, 390
```

kinds.point: #L3: lines count from 1, output lines included
kinds.reveal: lines up to the last range pointed at
kinds.format: Lines starting with a prompt ($, % or >) are commands; the rest is output. Paste real output, trimmed.

kinds.use: where files live in a project
kinds.point: #path/to/file, or a file or folder name that is unique in the tree
kinds.format: One entry per line, nested by indentation or pasted from `tree`. A trailing / marks a folder; `# note` after an entry shows a short note. Show only what matters.
kinds.example:
```tree
src/
  app.py   # entry point
  cache/
    lru.py
tests/
```

kinds.use: one to four headline numbers; each counts up from zero by itself, so `before -> after` only for a real change, not a total as `0 -> 300 million` or `3 -> 3`
kinds.reveal: numbers in source order; each counts up when pointed at, or at the slide's start if none are
kinds.format: One `label: value` or `label: before -> after` line per number. Values may carry a unit (`420 ms`, `2.1%`). `:icon:` before a label shows an icon beside it (`:clock: p95 latency: 420 ms`).
kinds.example:
```stat
p95 latency: 420 ms -> 180 ms
error rate: 2.1% -> 0.3%
```

kinds.use: a conversation, a prompt and its answer, a request and its response
kinds.format: One message per `name: text` line; indented lines continue the message above. A user, client or browser sits on the right; otherwise the second speaker does. At most 8 messages.
kinds.example:
```chat
user: How do I undo my last commit?
assistant: Run `git reset --soft HEAD~1`.
```

kinds.fence: ```svg, or ```svg file=path with an empty body; add step for versions that move, sketch for a hand-drawn look (```svg step sketch)
kinds.use: something physical, spatial or visual: light, an orbit, a lens, a molecule, a circuit, a geometric proof, a screen layout
kinds.point: #id of any element; an element's <title> or own text, or its slug (#air-molecule); #@left,top,width,height a region in percent of the drawing; [label](# "text") finds drawn text; add {.zoom} for small parts; with step versions, #step-2 moves to version 2
kinds.reveal: with .build, the outermost elements with ids, in source order; a cue at an id nested inside one reveals that part; unfilled strokes (rays, arrows, outlines) draw themselves in
kinds.format: One <svg> with a viewBox (0 0 1150 560 landscape, 0 0 860 800 square, 0 0 640 1080 portrait). Kept: shapes, paths, text, groups, gradients, markers, clip paths, masks, filters, <style> rules, <title>. Give each thing the narration names its own <g id="…">, in the order named. Removed (svg_removed): scripts, event handlers, links outside the drawing, foreignObject (embedded HTML), SMIL animation. For an existing .svg, ```svg file=path, empty body.
kinds.details: The viewBox shape for the frame fills the slide; in it, font-size 24 or more reads well, and text under about 12 px on the slide is flagged (text_too_small). file= reads an SVG from the project, such as an export from Excalidraw or Inkscape; for a .drawio or .drawio.svg file use ```drawio, whose cues reach its cells. Removed parts are reported; motion comes from reveals, cues and step versions. Use real colours where colour carries meaning; otherwise theme colours, which follow light and dark: var(--fg) for text and outlines, var(--muted), var(--accent), var(--line), var(--panel) for fills, var(--stage) for the slide background, and six palette colours var(--c1) to var(--c6) to tell parts apart. Icons: <use href="icon:database" x="40" y="40" width="64"/> draws a Lucide icon 64 units wide, stroked in the text colour or its own stroke=; ids, <title> and cues work on it as on any part. Step versions: consecutive ```svg step blocks on one slide are versions of one drawing. At #step-N, elements that keep their id glide to version N over about 1.2 s: numbers in attributes move, also inside a transform, path d or points list written the same way in both versions; hex and rgb() colours blend; other values and an element's text switch halfway; style= does not glide. Ids new in the version fade in, ids it dropped fade out. So keep the same ids across versions for what moves, put moving values in attributes, and write a transform alike in each (rotate(0 575 280), then rotate(-90 575 280)). To move along a circle, rotate a group around the centre instead of changing its x and y. Sketch: ```svg sketch redraws shapes by hand, as on a whiteboard (wobbly outlines, hatched fills, solid for small shapes, dashes kept), with text in a hand-drawn face; gradient fills stay as drawn. It combines with step; optional, suits informal explainers. Across slides: `.morph` on the next slide's heading, with an ```svg drawing on both, makes its drawing start as the previous one and glide into its own as the slide begins (same rules: keep ids for what moves).
kinds.example:
```svg
<svg viewBox="0 0 1150 560">
  <g id="sun"><circle cx="140" cy="140" r="70" fill="#ffd166"/><text x="140" y="260" font-size="28" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">Sun</text></g>
  <g id="air"><title>Air molecule</title><path d="M215 165 L560 260" stroke="var(--fg)" stroke-width="6" fill="none"/><circle cx="580" cy="266" r="18" fill="var(--muted)"/></g>
  <g id="blue"><title>Scattered blue</title><path d="M595 280 L880 450" stroke="#4f8cff" stroke-width="8" fill="none"/><text x="895" y="490" font-size="28" fill="var(--fg)">Your eye</text></g>
</svg>
```

kinds.fence: ```drawio file=path [page="Name" or page=2], with an empty body
kinds.use: a diagram the project already has as a draw.io file (.drawio, .drawio.xml, .drawio.svg); for a new picture, draw ```svg
kinds.point: #cell-id, or a cell's label or its slug when unique (#Postgres, #api-server); #@left,top,width,height a region in percent of the diagram; [label](# "text") finds label text; add {.zoom} for small parts
kinds.reveal: with .build, shapes directly on a layer in source order; a cue at a shape inside a container reveals the container; an edge appears once both its ends are shown
kinds.format: ```drawio file=path with an empty body reads one page of a draw.io file from the project: .drawio or .drawio.xml (plain or compressed), or a .drawio.svg export. page= picks a page by name or by number from 1; the first page is the default, and an unknown page lists the pages. Cue a cell by its id, read from the file (a wrong id lists the ids), or by a label that is unique on the page. For a new picture, draw ```svg instead.
kinds.details: A .drawio.svg export carries its diagram, so it reads like a .drawio file. The bundled draw.io viewer draws the page offline on a white page, scaled to fit the slide. Labels keep simple formatting (bold, italics, line breaks, lists, tables, colours); links, tooltips, placeholders, web fonts, images that are not embedded and maths are dropped. Shapes from icon libraries (AWS, Azure, GCP, Cisco and similar) are not bundled and show as plain boxes. More than 400 shapes and connectors is flagged (block_too_big): show one page or split it.

kinds.use: a card that opens a part of a long walkthrough, numbered Part 1, Part 2, …
kinds.format: A heading with .chapter and an optional `>` line under it; narration is optional.
kinds.example:
## The write path {.chapter}
> Where data lands

styles.circle: a hand-drawn ring around the target
styles.highlight: a marker stroke swept across it, left to right; the previous one fades about a second later
styles.zoom: the camera moves onto the target, easing in over about 1.5 s and settling as the cued word is heard, and holds there until the next cue; a cue without zoom, or # (the whole visual), pulls it back. Combine with another style. On a dense drawing, draw.io diagram or screenshot, zoom onto each part as it is named, then cue # to pull back to the whole; a zoom onto a large part, such as one panel of a grid, fills the frame without a pointer
styles.decode: the target's label shows scrambled from the start of the slide until this cue, then resolves left to right as the word is heard: for the answer the narration builds to. Cue an id: a drawing part, a diagram node, a list item or a table row

layouts.syntax: classes on the heading, as in ## Title {.side}; one layout per slide

layouts.default: title and an optional `>` line under it as a takeaway, the visual filling the rest
layouts..side: the visual on the left, one to three `>` lines beside it as takeaways (each may start with :icon:); for code, a diagram or a drawing that needs a reading guide
layouts..pair: two visuals side by side under one title, each written as usual: code and the diagram of what it does, before and after, a screenshot and its numbers. Cues point into either; ids must differ between them. No .build
layouts..full: the visual edge to edge, the title small in a corner: big drawings, diagrams, screenshots, charts
layouts.statement: a slide with no visual: its `>` line is shown as one large sentence, the heading a small kicker above it; for a claim, a definition, a turning point
layouts..morph: on an ```svg slide after another ```svg slide: the drawing glides from the previous slide's (see svg)

layouts.icons: Lucide icon names (lucide.dev), as :name: before a list item, stat label or `>` line, {icon=name} on a title, chapter or statement heading, or <use href="icon:name"/> in a drawing. Unknown names are reported with close ones (icon_unknown).
layouts.motion: slides start coming in just before their first word; they rise in, alike slides in a row slide across like pages, title and chapter slides zoom in, and cards, numbers, rows and takeaways arrive one after another, a tenth of a second apart. A still drawing breathes slightly and a held close-up creeps in, so a picture never freezes. All of it follows the narration's clock and shows in MP4 export, except the breathing and creep; reduced motion turns it off.
